xBRIEFInfo.author: overdeck/0.0.0
xBRIEFInfo.description: Plan for PAN-1166: Re-introduce /ws/terminal auth gate with a working bootstrap path

plan.title: Re-introduce /ws/terminal auth gate with a working bootstrap path
plan.author: agent:claude-opus-5-5

narratives.Problem: /ws/terminal, /ws/rpc, /ws/voice and /ws/autopreso authorize upgrades by origin only, and validateOriginHeaders passes a GET with no Origin header. The API binds 0.0.0.0, so any LAN client that omits Origin gets a live PTY on /ws/terminal and full RPC on /ws/rpc. The PAN-457 cookie gate was removed in 2026-05 because it broke Traefik terminals; two of its three root causes (no zero-step mint, per-boot session token) are fixed on main, and the third (frontend silently swallows a mint 401 at wsTransport.ts:80) remains.
narratives.Proposal: Add one shared authorizer, authorizeDashboardUpgrade in src/dashboard/server/ws-auth.ts (origin -> 403, no internal token -> 503, hasDashboardAuthHeaders cookie-or-internal-token -> 401), and route all four WebSocket endpoints through it. Peer trust stays only in the session mint. On the frontend, make ensureDashboardSession reject with a typed DashboardSessionUnauthorizedError on any 401, surface it as a new 'unauthorized' connection phase with a banner pointing at docs/DASHBOARD-AUTH.md, and make XTerminal and the voice/autopreso hooks await the mint before opening sockets. Document the threat model, including what the gate does not close (local processes; Traefik on all interfaces, PAN-4299). Prove it with unit tests per endpoint and a Playwright spec on an isolated dashboard.
narratives.NonGoals:
- Scoped access tokens on upgrades (?token=, verifyAccessToken, per-surface scopes, the read:events -> 403 matrix) — deferred to PAN-2351
- require_token_mint config — deferred to PAN-2351
- Trusting a loopback/Docker-bridge peer directly on WebSocket upgrades
- Gating HTTP GET read routes (GET /api/agents and siblings)
- Binding the API to 127.0.0.1 instead of 0.0.0.0
- Changing Traefik port publishing (PAN-4299)
- Changing the knowledge-viewer WebSocket proxy, which has its own access-token gate
- Changing the reauth one-time-token flow
- Widening session cookie attributes (Domain=, SameSite=Lax)
- Rate limiting
- Carrying any credential in a WebSocket URL
- Restarting or reloading the operator's live dashboard from the workspace

autoDecisions.summary: Ship the WebSocket gate without PAN-2351 scoped tokens; leave a single extension-point comment in ws-auth.ts
autoDecisions.rationale: PAN-2351 is OPEN with no code (git grep verifyAccessToken src is empty). The LAN PTY hole is live now, and the authorizer has one obvious place for 2351 to add ?token= scopes. An unmet dependency is not a contradiction between inputs.

autoDecisions.summary: Upgrade credential is session cookie OR internal token only; the authorizer never consults isLoopbackPeer
autoDecisions.rationale: Keeps peer trust in exactly one place (the session mint), so PAN-2351's require_token_mint closes it everywhere. Loopback browsers already auto-mint, so standard flows are unaffected.

autoDecisions.summary: Include /ws/autopreso in the gate even though the issue does not name it
autoDecisions.rationale: Issue acceptance criterion #4 forbids a half-gated state; /ws/autopreso was added after the issue was written and uses the same origin-only pattern.

autoDecisions.summary: Any 401 from either mint host (PAN-3711 two-host mint) rejects ensureDashboardSession
autoDecisions.rationale: XTerminal connects to window.location.host, which can be the second host, so a 401 there means a socket will fail.

autoDecisions.summary: Relax /ws/voice and /ws/autopreso to validateOriginHeaders (absent Origin allowed through to the credential check)
autoDecisions.rationale: One origin rule for all four endpoints; a credential-less request still gets 401, and browsers always send Origin on upgrades, so cross-site hijacking stays blocked.

autoDecisions.summary: Do not fix Traefik all-interface port publishing here; filed PAN-4299 and document it in the threat model
autoDecisions.rationale: It is a pre-existing template change with its own blast radius (LAN/device access to workspace stacks).

autoDecisions.summary: Restart-stability of the session cookie needs no new work
autoDecisions.rationale: The HMAC derivation already exists (dashboard-auth.ts:43-46) and is locked by dashboard-auth.test.ts:51.

narrative.Action: PRD W1. Create src/dashboard/server/ws-auth.ts exporting authorizeDashboardUpgrade(headers: HeaderMap, method: string): { ok: true } | { ok: false; status: 401|403|503; message } and rejectUpgrade(socket, status, message), exactly as the PRD W1 snippet: validateOriginHeaders -> 403; getInternalToken() empty -> 503; hasDashboardAuthHeaders(headers) false -> 401 'Unauthorized'. Do NOT consult isLoopbackPeer (FR-3). Keep one comment line at the credential step: '// PAN-2351 adds scoped access tokens (?token=) here.' Module header comment names FR-1/FR-3 and points to docs/DASHBOARD-AUTH.md. Add src/dashboard/server/__tests__/ws-auth.test.ts with the 8 cases listed in PRD W1.

narrative.Action: PRD W12. Add src/dashboard/frontend/tests/pan-1166-ws-auth.spec.ts using startIsolatedDashboard from ./fixtures/isolated-dashboard.js (pattern: tests/pan-4279-degraded-mode.spec.ts; never the live :3011 dashboard). Run 'npm run build' first. Four journeys, each in a fresh browser context: (1) zero-step bootstrap — load with no hash, context.cookies() has overdeck_session, no unauthorized banner, take and inspect a screenshot; (2) gate present — Node ws client upgrades /ws/terminal?session=x, /ws/rpc, /ws/voice, /ws/autopreso with the fixture Origin and no cookie, each gets unexpected-response 401; (3) cookie accepted — same upgrades with the journey-1 cookie are accepted; (4) loud 401 — route.fulfill({ status: 401 }) on POST **/api/dashboard/session shows data-phase="unauthorized" or the first-load heading 'Dashboard session could not be established'. Implementation checkpoint (PRD W12): if a workspace dev stack with VITE_API_URL on a different host is available, verify a terminal connects there; if it does not, record the host pair in the PR description and file a follow-up issue — do not widen cookie attributes.

metadata.sizeJustification: 27 files across 4 subsystems (src/dashboard, scripts, docs x2). Issue acceptance criterion #4 forbids a half-gated state, so all four WebSocket endpoint gates must ship in one change, and the client mint-before-connect ordering (wsTransport, XTerminal, voice/autopreso hooks) must ship with them or terminals break the moment the gate is on. Splitting into sibling issues would leave main either half-gated or with a gate the client cannot pass. 12 of the 27 files are test files (9 new, one per slice).
